statement: Autologous epidermal stem cells corrected with a retroviral vector regenerated a durable, functional, self-renewing epidermis in patients with junctional epidermolysis bullosa: nine grafts on an adult's legs stable at one year (2006), and an entire epidermis on ~80% of a child's body surface (2017).

context.intervention: ex vivo retroviral LAMB3 correction of epidermal stem cells; cultured grafts

measurement.assay: clinical follow-up; integration-site analysis; clonal tracing
measurement.effect: full functional correction of grafted areas; maintained by a defined repertoire of transduced stem cells

replication.note: Both patients treated by the same group (De Luca). Two successes, no independent replication — L4, not L5.

drift: 'Boy given new skin' — the regenerated organ is the epidermis; the dermis was his own.
wouldMove: An unaffiliated centre reproducing durable engraftment, with integration-site surveillance beyond five years.

provenance.method: manual reasoning from the cited sources' abstracts (PubMed) and Crossref metadata, checked 2026-09-11; no source opened at figure level
